caption_modes.trigger_only: Trigger only (minimal, common for Flux characters)

character.name: Character
character.desc: Teach the trigger a specific character's or person's look.
tips: Use 15–50 images with different angles, expressions, outfits and backgrounds; avoid many near-identical shots.
Remove tags for the character's fixed traits (hair color, eye color…) so they get bound to the trigger; keep tags for things that vary (outfit, expression, action).
If you want to change hairstyle / hair color freely later, don't remove those tags.
If WD14 detects an existing character tag for the character you are training, remove it and rely on your own trigger.

style.name: Style
style.desc: Teach the model an art or photo style; the content still comes from the prompt.
tips: Use 50–200+ images with varied content (people, scenery, objects…) but a consistent style.
Tags should only describe what is drawn: remove style / medium tags (anime coloring, sketch, watercolor…) so the trigger absorbs the style.
Always remove artist-name tags. A trigger like `xyz style` works well.

concept.name: Concept / Object
concept.desc: Poses, actions, outfits, objects, compositions and other concepts.
tips: Use 20–100 images; everything other than the concept (people, backgrounds) should vary as much as possible.
Remove the tags that directly describe the concept so the trigger represents it; keep all other tags.
Outfit LoRA: remove the outfit's component tags (e.g. serafuku, pleated skirt) and keep character traits such as hair color.

prune_groups.body: Body features (ears, horns, tail, chest, skin tone…)
prune_groups.nsfw: NSFW tags (only when making an SFW version)

bulk_actions.reapply: Regenerate tags from the raw WD14 scores using the current threshold / prune / blacklist settings (overwrites manual edits)
bulk_actions.filter: Apply prune groups and blacklist to the existing tags (keeps manual edits)

server.nsfw_common: WD14 outputs Danbooru NSFW tags uncensored; to make an SFW version, tick the “NSFW tags” prune group. Keep `censored` / `mosaic censoring` / `uncensored` tags so you can control them at generation time. Per Civitai policy, images combining minor-like traits with sexual content are flagged and excluded from export automatically.

sd15_anime.name: SD 1.5 Anime (NAI / Anything / Counterfeit / MeinaMix)
sd15_anime.summary: Danbooru tags, 75-token CLIP limit, trigger first.
sd15_anime.civitai_base: SD 1.5 (or the matching anime base model)
sd15_anime.caption_style: Use Danbooru tags separated by “, ” with underscores replaced by spaces. SD1.5's CLIP reads only 75 tokens at a time, so aim for 20–35 tags per image with the important ones first.
sd15_anime.a1111_settings: Sampler: DPM++ 2M Karras / Euler a, Steps 25–30, CFG 7, 512×768, Clip skip 2
sd15_anime.nsfw: NAI-based models separate adult content with the `nsfw` tag: images rated questionable / explicit get `nsfw` automatically, and WD14's Danbooru NSFW tags (nipples, pussy, sex…) are kept. For SFW generations put `nsfw` in the negative prompt.
notes: In A1111 prompts parentheses mean emphasis, so a character tag like `tokai teio (umamusume)` must be written `tokai teio \(umamusume\)` in the prompt; no escaping is needed in training .txt files.
Quality tags (masterpiece etc.) usually should not go into training captions, or they get bound to your dataset.

sd15_realistic.name: SD 1.5 Realistic (Realistic Vision / majicMIX / epiCRealism)
sd15_realistic.summary: Short sentence + key tags, with the trigger as the subject (e.g. ohwx woman).
sd15_realistic.civitai_base: SD 1.5 (or the matching realistic base model)
sd15_realistic.caption_style: Most realistic models were trained on LAION-style short sentences: one sentence for the subject and scene, then a few key tags. Use a rare token plus a class word as the trigger, e.g. `ohwx woman`.
sd15_realistic.a1111_settings: Sampler: DPM++ 2M Karras / DPM++ SDE Karras, Steps 25–35, CFG 5–7, 512×768, Clip skip 1
sd15_realistic.nsfw: Realistic models also use `nsfw`. For the VLM, enable “Explicit NSFW descriptions” and use an uncensored model (JoyCaption); otherwise descriptions are often refused or vague.
notes: WD14 is an anime model and is less accurate on real photos — enable the VLM for sentences and use WD14 only as a supplement.
For portrait LoRAs, crop so faces are clear and vary the lighting.

sdxl_base.name: SDXL 1.0 / Realistic XL (Juggernaut XL / RealVisXL)
sdxl_base.summary: SDXL's dual CLIP understands natural language better: 1–2 sentences + a few tags.
sdxl_base.caption_style: Describe the subject, action, outfit, scene, lighting and camera in 1–2 natural-language sentences, then add a few key tags. Put the trigger at the start.

training.te_lr: 0 ~ 5e-5 (the TE is often left untrained on SDXL)

sdxl_base.a1111_settings: Sampler: DPM++ 2M Karras / DPM++ SDE, Steps 30, CFG 4–7, 1024×1024 / 832×1216
sdxl_base.nsfw: Base SDXL has limited NSFW ability; for adult LoRAs train on Pony / Illustrious / NoobAI or an NSFW fine-tune. NSFW images get `nsfw`.
notes: Use images of at least 1024px for SDXL datasets; small images lower the quality.

pony_v6.name: Pony Diffusion V6 XL
pony_v6.summary: Danbooru/e621 tags + source_* and rating_* tags; score tags at generation time, Clip skip 2.
pony_v6.caption_style: Use Danbooru tags (underscores → spaces), prefixed with a source tag `source_anime` / `source_cartoon` / `source_furry` / `source_pony` and a rating tag `rating_safe` / `rating_questionable` / `rating_explicit`.
pony_v6.a1111_settings: Sampler: Euler a / DPM++ 2M Karras, Steps 25, CFG 6–7, 1024×1024 / 832×1216, Clip skip 2
pony_v6.nsfw: Pony controls explicitness with rating tags: `rating_safe` / `rating_questionable` / `rating_explicit` (added automatically from the WD14 rating). For SFW generations put `rating_explicit` in the negative prompt; otherwise put it in the positive.
notes: Training captions usually do NOT include score_9 and similar quality tags; if your dataset is exceptionally good you can enable score_9 in the settings.
Rating tags are converted automatically from the WD14 rating.

illustrious.name: Illustrious XL (v0.1 / v1 / v2) and derivatives (WAI etc.)
illustrious.summary: Pure Danbooru tags, ordered count → character → series → artist → general tags.
illustrious.caption_style: Mainly Danbooru tags (underscores → spaces). Versions from v1.0 on also understand short sentences, so “Hybrid” mode is an option. Use the official Danbooru spelling for character and series names.
illustrious.nsfw: Illustrious can use the rating tags `general` / `sensitive` / `nsfw` / `explicit` (off by default; turn on “Add rating tags” for NSFW datasets). Danbooru NSFW tags are kept as-is.
notes: Illustrious derivatives (WAI-NSFW-illustrious etc.) are captioned the same way.
LoRAs trained on Illustrious usually also work on NoobAI models (compatible, though colors may shift).

noobai_xl.name: NoobAI-XL (eps / v-pred)
noobai_xl.summary: Based on Illustrious; Danbooru + e621 tags, rating tags general / sensitive / nsfw / explicit.
noobai_xl.civitai_base: NoobAI (choose Illustrious if it is not listed)
noobai_xl.caption_style: Danbooru tags (underscores → spaces) with optional rating tags. Suggested order: count → character → series → artist → general tags.
noobai_xl.a1111_settings: Sampler: Euler a (eps) / Euler (v-pred), Steps 28, CFG 4–5, 1024×1024 / 832×1216
noobai_xl.nsfw: NoobAI's rating tags are `general` / `sensitive` / `nsfw` / `explicit` (on by default); Danbooru / e621 NSFW tags are kept as-is.
notes: The v-pred version needs a WebUI with v-prediction support (Forge / reForge / A1111 dev); when training with kohya yourself add --v_parameterization --zero_terminal_snr.
Tagging works the same as for Illustrious.

animagine_xl.name: Animagine XL 3.1 / 4.0
animagine_xl.summary: Fixed order: count → character → series → rating → other tags; ratings safe / sensitive / nsfw / explicit.
animagine_xl.caption_style: Animagine's official tag structure is `1girl/1boy, character, series, rating, other tags`, optionally followed by quality and year tags.
animagine_xl.nsfw: Animagine's rating tags are `safe` / `sensitive` / `nsfw` / `explicit` (on by default), placed after the character / series.
notes: Animagine 4.0's quality tags differ from 3.1's (3.1: masterpiece, best quality, very aesthetic).

anima.name: Anima (Base / Aesthetic / Turbo)
anima.summary: Danbooru tags (sentences / mixed also work), safety tag first, artists need @; runs in ComfyUI / Forge Neo, not A1111.
anima.caption_style: Lowercase Danbooru tags with spaces instead of underscores (only score_* tags keep underscores). Anima was also trained on natural-language captions and tag + sentence mixes, so “Hybrid” mode works too. Order: quality / meta / year / safety tags → 1girl / 1boy → character → series → artist → general tags; order inside each section doesn't matter. The Qwen3 text encoder reads up to 512 tokens, so there is no 75-token CLIP limit.

training.lr: diffusion-pipe: 2e-5 for rank 32 (official starting point); sd-scripts: 1e-4 at the default alpha 1 — lower it as alpha grows
training.text_encoder: Usually not trained (--network_train_unet_only + --cache_text_encoder_outputs); never train the LLM adapter
training.steps: No official number — save every epoch (sd-scripts example: 10 epochs) and pick the best
training.shuffle: Off (sd-scripts forbids shuffle_caption with --cache_text_encoder_outputs; caption_dropout_rate still works)

anima.a1111_settings: ComfyUI (native) / Forge Neo: sampler er_sde (neutral default) / euler_a / dpmpp_2m_sde, steps 30–50, CFG 4–5, 1024×1024 / 832×1216; Anima-Turbo: CFG 1, 8–12 steps. Stock A1111 is not supported.
anima.nsfw: Anima puts the safety tags `safe` / `sensitive` / `nsfw` / `explicit` at the front of the prompt (converted from the WD14 rating, on by default). Short prompts can drift into unwanted content, so for SFW generations put `safe` in the positive and `nsfw, explicit` in the negative.
notes: Train LoRAs on Anima-Base, not Aesthetic / Turbo; a LoRA trained on Base also works with the other versions.
Don't train the LLM adapter: diffusion-pipe uses llm_adapter_lr=0 in its example config; sd-scripts leaves it out of the LoRA unless train_llm_adapter=True.
Artist tags must start with @ (e.g. `@nnn yryr`), otherwise their effect is very weak. WD14 does not output artist tags; keep artist names out of style-LoRA captions.
When Danbooru and Gelbooru spell a tag differently, Anima prefers the Gelbooru version.
Prompt weights need to be higher than on SDXL, e.g. `(chibi:2)`. In ComfyUI load the LoRA with a LoraLoader node; `<lora:…>` works in Forge Neo.

flux1_dev.name: FLUX.1 [dev]
flux1_dev.summary: T5 text encoder → detailed natural language, no caption shuffling; not supported by A1111 — use Forge / ComfyUI.
flux1_dev.caption_style: Write complete, objective natural-language descriptions (2–5 sentences): subject, appearance, outfit, action, expression, background, composition, camera, lighting and style. Use the trigger as the subject's name inside the sentence. T5 reads up to 512 tokens.
flux1_dev.a1111_settings: Forge / ComfyUI: sampler Euler, scheduler Simple, steps 20–30, distilled CFG 3.5, CFG 1, 1024×1024
flux1_dev.a1111_negative_note: (Flux dev does not use a negative prompt)
flux1_dev.nsfw: Flux.1 dev has weak native NSFW ability, so captions must describe bodies and actions plainly in natural language: enable “Explicit NSFW descriptions” and use an uncensored VLM such as JoyCaption; Claude and other commercial models will refuse.
notes: Stock AUTOMATIC1111 does not support Flux; use Stable Diffusion WebUI Forge or ComfyUI.
For character LoRAs you can also try trigger-only captions — Flux often learns well from them, but you get less control.

h.trigger: Placed at the very start of every caption
h.class_word: Used by trigger-only mode and kohya folder names
h.use_wd14: WD14 outputs NSFW tags (nude, nipples, sex…) and the rating without any filtering; the rating is converted to this base model's format (Anima: safe / sensitive / nsfw / explicit). Only tick the “NSFW tags” prune group if you want an SFW version.
h.vlm_tags: Best with JoyCaption (built-in Danbooru mode; officially about 3% of outputs glitch). Unless Off, the VLM is called regardless of “Enable VLM descriptions” — one extra VLM call per image. VLMs often invent character and series names, so when WD14 already recognizes a character and the VLM disagrees, the VLM's character / series tags are ignored. VLM tags have no confidence scores, so thresholds only apply to WD14.
h.vlm_artist_tags: VLMs often guess artists wrong; leave this off for style LoRAs. Anima adds the @ prefix automatically.
h.use_vlm: Used in natural / hybrid mode. Current: {status}
h.vlm_nsfw: Allows plain adult vocabulary; needs an uncensored model (e.g. JoyCaption) — Claude and most commercial models refuse
h.include_rating: Converted from the WD14 rating to this model's format (recommended for NSFW datasets)
h.add_quality_tags: Usually not recommended — binds quality to your dataset
h.escape_parentheses: Usually not needed in training captions
h.block_tag_auto: White rectangles used to cover other people get learned into the LoRA unless the caption names them. With this on, images with white blocks get the keyword at the end of the caption; put it in the negative prompt when generating.
h.block_tag: Default “white rectangle”. Changing it applies to every caption right away.

settings.warn_vlm_ignored: “Enable VLM descriptions” is on, but this caption mode only uses tags, so the VLM will not be called. Switch to Natural language / Hybrid to add VLM descriptions.
settings.warn_rating_needs_wd14: Rating tags come from WD14; with WD14 off no rating tags are added.
settings.warn_natural_tags_unused: In Natural language mode the caption is only the VLM's sentences: WD14 tags (including NSFW tags) are not written to the caption — they only guide the VLM and provide the rating. Switch to Hybrid to keep the tags as well.

civitai.views: Training amount: {steps} steps × batch {batch} ÷ {n} images ≈ each image seen {views} times
civitai.views_low: That is low — details that appear only in some images (outfits, accessories) may not be learned. About {suggest} steps would show each image ~{target} times.
civitai.priority_help: The civitai.com trainer's High Priority switch sends Normal: it is queued ahead of Low and, per Civitai, runs uninterrupted. What High does depends on your account tier. The estimate shows the price for the chosen priority.
civitai.cost_full: This estimate includes a Civitai discount. The undiscounted price is {full} Buzz, and the final charge may settle at that amount, so keep enough Buzz.
civitai.cancel_no_refund: No refund recorded so far (Civitai only documents refunds for work that had not started).
civitai.cancel_pending: Cancel sent at {time}. Civitai shows “Canceled” only after the training machine stops, which can take a few minutes; any refund will appear here.
civitai.cancel_sent: Cancel sent. The run changes to “Canceled” once Civitai stops the training (this can take a few minutes).
civitai.force_upload_help: Usually not needed: captions are sent with every training request, so editing tags never needs a re-upload, and images cropped or replaced here are re-uploaded automatically. Only tick this when image files were changed outside this app, or to have Civitai moderate them again.
civitai.retrain_filled: Filled in the settings of the run from {when} (including the sample prompts). Your current tags will be used; click “{button}” when ready.
civitai.retrain_unknown_type: This app does not support that run's training type ({type}), so its settings cannot be filled in.

api.title: API / MCP — for other LLMs
api.auth_on_html: API_KEY is enabled on the server: send Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY> (or X-API-Key) with every request.
api.auth_off_html: API_KEY is not set, so anyone who can reach this server can use the API. Set it in .env before exposing the server.
api.mcp_title: MCP (Claude Desktop / Claude Code / Cursor / Open WebUI)
api.mcp_http_clients: Cursor / VS Code / clients with HTTP support
api.openwebui_html: Open WebUI: Settings → External tools → Add → type MCP (Streamable HTTP), URL {url}.
api.openapi_desc: Every REST endpoint has an operation_id and a description, so the spec can be imported directly as function-calling tools (Open WebUI OpenAPI tool servers, GPT Actions, the LangChain OpenAPI toolkit…).
api.lang_html: Guides and messages follow the ?lang= parameter, the X-Lang header or Accept-Language (zh-TW, en, ja, ko, zh-CN); MCP uses the server's DEFAULT_LANG.
api.step2: 2. Upload images / zip (same-name .txt files become existing captions)
